first_impression.reaction: Fair opening. It says straight up that most guides are written for Brits and Americans and that the Certificate of No Impediment won't work in Italy. That's a specific claim I can check against the Embassy, and they say they're current as at October 2026. Good enough to keep going. As usual I jumped to the costs section and the FAQ first, then went back to the steps.

journey.quote: Most guides online are written for British or American couples and talk about a Certificate of No Impediment, which Italy will not accept from you.
journey.reaction: Specific and checkable. If that holds up, it's already saved me from following the wrong guide.

journey.quote: Atto Notorio: a consular fee applies, set by each consulate's tariff.
journey.reaction: This is the first thing I read and there's not one dollar figure in it. Every line is 'a fee applies'. The consular and DFAT fees are published by the government, so why not give me the number, or at least a ballpark with a date on it? Linking to DFAT's fee page is something, but the section reads like it's dodging.

journey.quote: Not published: interpreter and translation rates. Your Wedded Advisor costs the full paperwork in AUD for your comune.
journey.reaction: So the only way I get an actual number is to talk to their salesperson. That's the catch I was looking for. And the bigger question: if your Advisor costs the interpreter and translator, are those your mark-ups or the supplier's price?

journey.quote: Brisbane advises the fee after reviewing your documents and accepts cash only.
journey.reaction: Useful, and it's my consulate. Cash only is exactly the kind of thing that catches you out on the day.

journey.quote: No. The Embassy says Certificates of No Impediment are not valid for use in Italy.
journey.reaction: Short, sourced, answers the question. The FAQ is tight. No fluff.

journey.quote: Appointment lead times are not published, so book before you fly.
journey.reaction: Honest that they don't know, which I respect. But it's the question I'd most want answered and it isn't. 'Book before you fly' isn't a number.

journey.quote: Brisbane wants first contact at least one month before you fly, and witnesses who have known you for at least 12 months.
journey.reaction: This is the bit that's actually useful to me. Consulate-by-consulate detail is something you only get if someone has read the sources. The 12-month witness rule is something I'd never have guessed.

journey.section: Birth certificate and single status certificate
journey.quote: Queensland residents provide a Letter of No Record of Marriage instead, and Northern Territory residents a Letter of No Impediment.
journey.reaction: Another Queensland-specific detail. That tells me they've done the work and haven't just copied a Sydney checklist.

journey.section: Why a Certificate of No Impediment will not work in Italy
journey.quote: "Nulla Ostas sworn outside of Italy and Certificates of No Impediment are not valid for use in Italy."
journey.reaction: A direct quote from the Embassy, with the PDF linked further up. That's the kind of proof I want.

journey.quote: On Sydney's list, two Australians with two certificates and two translations each can need eight apostilles.
journey.reaction: Good. Now give me the per-apostille fee and I can do the maths myself. As it stands I know the count but not the cost.

journey.section: Step by step once you arrive in Italy
journey.quote: Rome's office opens Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, 9am to 12pm.
journey.reaction: Actual days and hours. I can plan a week around that. More of this, please.

journey.section: Can Australians legally get married in Italy?
journey.quote: Rules change, so your Wedded Advisor confirms the current requirements for your date and comune.
journey.reaction: First of many. I lost count of 'your Wedded Advisor confirms' after about eight. Once or twice is fine. Every section is a sales hook, and there's still no word on what that Advisor costs or who pays them.

journey.section: Is an Italian marriage recognised in Australia?
journey.quote: One catch if you are changing your name. In NSW and Victoria, an overseas marriage certificate cannot be used to take your spouse's surname, so you apply for a change of name instead.
journey.reaction: They actually point out a catch themselves. That's rare. It also hedges properly with 'in most cases' instead of overselling.

journey.section: Your timeline, working back from the wedding date
journey.quote: The squeeze is in the middle. Both documents expire six months after signing, so a date that moves late can mean signing again.
journey.reaction: Honest about the risk. The table is the most useful thing on the page. I'd screenshot it.

journey.section: Plan the paperwork with one person
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and stays with you from the first document to the last dance.
journey.reaction: 'From the first document to the last dance' is the brochure voice creeping in. Doesn't bother me much, but it's the one line on the page that tells me nothing.

unanswered_questions: What does a Wedded Advisor cost? Flat fee, percentage of the budget, or free because you're paid by suppliers?
Do you take a commission or add a margin on venues, interpreters, translators or comune fees?
What are the actual dollar amounts for the Atto Notorio, Nulla Osta and DFAT apostille fees, as at a stated date?
How far ahead are Nulla Osta appointments in Rome or Milan actually available, even based on recent clients?
When the Advisor 'confirms in writing', what happens if that confirmation turns out to be wrong? Who wears the cost?
Is there a real example, with dates, of an Australian couple who went through this sequence?

turn_offs_found.quote: Prefettura: a fee applies as a revenue stamp (marca da bollo), bought at a tabaccaio before you go.
turn_offs_found.why: The whole cost section names fees without a single number. A section titled 'What the paperwork costs' should tell me what the paperwork costs.

turn_offs_found.quote: Not published: which private villas your comune approves for civil ceremonies. Your Wedded Advisor confirms in writing whether your venue qualifies before you sign with it.
turn_offs_found.why: Repeated 'your Wedded Advisor confirms' lines in nearly every section, with no mention of what the Advisor costs or how they're paid. It feels like the gaps are being kept as reasons to enquire.

turn_offs_found.quote: stays with you from the first document to the last dance.
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional filler instead of a fact about the service.

would_share_with: My partner, mainly for the timeline table
A mate in Brisbane who's also looking at Italy

cta_reaction.quote: Speak with a Wedded Advisor about your paperwork timeline, starting with your date and your comune.
cta_reaction.why: At least the CTA comes at the end, after real evidence, and it's specific about what we'd talk about. But I don't enquire until I know the fee model and whether there are kickbacks from suppliers, and the page doesn't say. I'd go and look for a pricing or 'how we're paid' page first. If I didn't find one, I wouldn't click.

top_3_changes: Put real numbers in the cost section: the published consular and DFAT fees in AUD with an 'as at' date, or at least a dated range. Right now it's five lines saying 'a fee applies'.
Add one or two sentences on how the Wedded Advisor is paid: what the fee is, and whether you take commission from venues, interpreters or translators. Link to it next to the CTA.
Cut 'your Wedded Advisor confirms' back to two or three places where it matters (Nulla Osta lead time, comune list, venue approval). Everywhere else it reads like a sales hook, not help.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): read costs and FAQ first, judged on proof, fees and commissions
No invented brand facts; missing fee model and commission details listed as unanswered questions
[[VERIFY]] markers and HTML comments treated as invisible
Did not invent problems; positives recorded where the draft earned them
